Q3 2026 Revenues
Record revenues, strong execution and full year target upgraded
Rueil-Malmaison (France), October 16th, 2026
Financial Highlights
• Revenues up +17% organic to €11.5 billion, a record high for any quarter
o Broad-based demand across end-markets, led by Data Center up triple-digit
o Strong growth in Energy Management, up +19% organic
o Continued momentum in Industrial Automation, up +8% organic
o All regions growing, led by China & East Asia up +26% org. and North America up +20% org.
o Accelerating price contributes to Product growth of +17% org.
• Sustainability Impact 2030 program underway, reaching a score of 4.04
• 2026 Financial Target upgraded
Olivier Blum, Chief Executive Officer, commented:
“We delivered record quarterly revenues of €11.5 billion in Q3, growing 17% organically, demonstrating
the strength of our value proposition across end-markets and geographies. Energy Management
delivered outstanding growth, while Industrial Automation maintained solid momentum. As
expected, Data Centers remained a key growth driver as we continue to execute on our backlog while
seeing triple-digit demand growth in the quarter, providing increasing visibility into 2027 and 2028.
More broadly, demand remained healthy across all four end-markets, supporting another record
backlog at quarter-end.
We are seeing strong execution across all our business models. Product growth benefited from both
proactive pricing actions and healthy volumes, Systems continued to perform strongly, and Software
& Services delivered another solid quarter.
Earlier this month, we announced the signing of a definitive agreement to acquire PTC, a
transformative step in advancing our vision of Energy and Industrial Intelligence. Together, we will
create a unique Software & AI powerhouse bridging the physical and digital worlds across all our
four end markets. By connecting and contextualizing data across the lifecycle of products and assets,
we will create a unique digital thread for the next generation of Industrial AI, helping customers to
optimize their systems with greater intelligence.
Our Q3 performance demonstrates the relentless focus, agility and execution of our teams across
the Group. While pursuing our long-term strategic ambitions, we remain firmly focused on
operational excellence and delivering for our customers every day. The strength of our results,
backlog and market positions gives us confidence in our ability to capture the opportunities ahead
while continuing to execute against our commitments. As a result, we are today upgrading our 2026
financial target.”

Page | 2
I. THIRD QUARTER REVENUES WERE UP +17% ORGANIC
2026 Q3 revenues were €11,460 million, up +16.9% organic and up +17.9% on a reported basis.
Q3 2026 PERFORMANCE BY BUSINESS MODEL
Products (48% of Q3 revenues) grew +17% organic in Q3. Growth was majority volume-driven, with
price increasing sequentially as expected, with actions taken at the start of the year now at full run-
rate and supplementary actions ramping up. Product revenues grew double-digit in Energy
Management, with broad-based growth in electrical power distribution across all four end-markets.
Products in Industrial Automation also grew double-digit, as the recovery in Discrete automation saw
sustained momentum, driving growth across multiple product categories.
Systems (35% of Q3 revenues) grew +22% organic in Q3. Energy Management was up strong double-
digit, with Data Center driving growth, notably in prefabricated solutions, continued strength in 3-
phase UPS and cooling. The Infrastructure end-market also saw strong growth, notably with Grid
customers. Industrial Automation grew low-single digit, seeing good growth with OEMs in Discrete
automation, while Process & Hybrid markets saw declines overall, impacted by weakness in China.
Software & Services (17% of Q3 revenues) grew +7% organic in Q3 of which Software & Digital Services
(7% of Q3 revenues) grew +8% organic and Field Services (10% of Q3 revenues) grew +7% organic.
Agnostic Software (comprising AVEVA, ETAP and RIB Software)
AVEVA delivered strong growth in Annualized Recurring Revenue (ARR), up +10% as of September
30, 2026 led by upsell to existing customers and supported by new logo wins including with
customers in Energy & Chemicals (E&C), Transport, Automotive and through distribution
channels. Organic revenue growth in Q3 was at similar levels to the ARR growth. Revenue
continues to be driven by strong growth in subscription, with cloud-based SaaS continuing to
grow significantly faster than on-premise rental. Subscription revenues further advanced as a
proportion of total revenues as AVEVA nears completion of its subscription transition.
Energy Management agnostic software offers (ETAP and RIB Software) grew mid-single digit
organic in the quarter, with strong growth in recurring revenues, while perpetual license
revenues declined as expected. Performance was differentiated, with ETAP seeing strong
organic growth despite a double-digit base of comparison, while organic growth at RIB Software
was more subdued, with both impacted by the ongoing subscription transition.
Services (comprising Digital and Field Services offers) grew high-single digit organic in Q3
Field Services grew +7% organic in Q3, with high-single digit growth in Energy Management and
mid-single digit growth in Industrial Automation. In Energy Management, growth was driven by
installation, commissioning and modernization activities in Data Center, supported by strong
traction for the Group’s recurring service plan offerings. Sales of the Group’s efficiency and
sustainability program offers declined due to demand weakness in previous quarters.
Digital Services delivered high-single digit organic growth in Q3 driven by EcoStruxure solutions
for Data Centers, Cybersecurity, Digital offers for Grid customers and Planon.

Financial Information
Page | 3
Q3 2026 PERFORMANCE BY END-MARKET
Schneider Electric sells its integrated portfolio into four end-markets: Data Center & Networks,
Buildings, Industry and Infrastructure, leveraging the unique combination of Energy Management and
Industrial Automation complementary offers and technologies supported by the focus on
electrification, automation and digitalization to enable a sustainable future.
• Data Center & Networks – The Data Center & Networks end-market delivered another quarter of
exceptionally strong demand, with Q3 demand up triple-digit. Demand within the pure Data Center
segment remained very strong, up triple-digit globally, with strong demand across all four regions,
led by North America, while demand in China & East Asia accelerated to a similar rate. Demand
remained broad-based across hyperscale, colocation, neo-cloud and edge customers, reflecting the
strength of the Group's comprehensive portfolio and global footprint. Sales growth in the pure Data
Center segment was again up strong double-digit, driven by the Group’s offer in prefabricated
solutions, electrical distribution & protection, and cooling. The Distributed IT segment saw strong
performance in the quarter, with orders and sales both up double-digit, supported by the strength of
the broader end-market.
• Buildings – The Buildings end-market saw strong demand in the quarter, driven mostly by strength
in Non-residential while Residential demand remains concentrated in specific countries, most notably
in India. Demand in Non-Residential was strong across most geographies, notably in the U.S., which
saw strong demand in public access & public administration buildings, and in parts of Europe, while
China remained weak. Sales followed a similar trend, with good growth in the Buildings end-market
overall, with Non-Residential remaining stronger than Residential in most major geographies apart
from India which also saw strength in Residential.
• Industry – Demand in the Industry end-market was strong, with Discrete automation benefiting from
sustained strong demand momentum, led by China, India and East Asia. Hybrid automation
segments, including Semiconductor and Consumer Packaged Goods also saw strong demand.
Demand in Process automation was contrasted by region, with strength in the Middle East and India,
both seeing traction in the E&C segment, good demand in North America while China was down and
Europe remained subdued. Sales into the Industry end-market saw solid growth overall, including
good growth in Discrete automation, and strong contribution from the Semiconductor segment in
specific geographies, such as East Asia. Process industries saw positive growth for a second
successive quarter, though not yet reflecting the strong demand of past quarters.
• Infrastructure – The Infrastructure end-market saw good demand in the quarter. Demand was
strongest in the Water & Wastewater (WWW) segment, primarily in North America, supported by large
service and efficiency projects with public utilities. Power & Grid (P&G) demand declined slightly
during the period, with sustained strong demand from Grid customers across several geographies
offset by declines in Power Generation. There was good demand momentum in the Transportation
segment, notably from Marine. The Infrastructure end-market saw good sales growth driven by the
Transportation and P&G segments, helped by sales of the Group’s SF6-free switchgear.

North America (40% of Q3 revenues) grew +19.9% organic in Q3.
Energy Management grew +20.3% organic. The U.S. was up strong double-digit, led by strong growth
in Data Center, which saw sustained customer demand for the Group’s comprehensive offers,
particularly prefabricated solutions and cooling. Growth in other end-markets was solid overall, led
by strong growth in Buildings, with continued traction in government-related, public-access and
commercial building segments. Industry and Infrastructure were down overall, though growth was
contrasted across segments, and included strong growth with Grid customers. Canada grew double-
digit led by Data Center and Infrastructure while Buildings remained weak, notably in Residential.
Mexico returned to growth, up double-digit against a low base of comparison, led by Buildings and
Data Center.
Industrial Automation grew +16.3% organic. There was strong double-digit growth in industrial
software at AVEVA which benefitted from contract renewals in E&C and strong growth through
distribution channels. Discrete automation also grew double-digit, accelerating strongly in the
quarter, while sales into Process & Hybrid automation declined slightly. The U.S. grew double-digit with
strong growth at AVEVA and for Discrete automation offers sold into Industrial Manufacturing, E&C
and across the Infrastructure end-market. Mid-single digit growth in Canada was led by Discrete
automation, with good traction across many industrial segments, and with good services delivery on
a project with an E&C customer. Mexico grew double-digit against a low base of comparison with
good contributions from Discrete automation offers in Industrial Manufacturing.

Financial Information
Page | 5
Europe (23% of Q3 revenues) grew +8.6% organic in Q3.
Energy Management grew +9.2% organic. Growth was led by the Data Center end-market, notably
with regional co-location customers embracing a fully integrated turnkey approach through the
Group’s prefabricated solutions. Infrastructure delivered strong growth driven by P&G where utility
partnerships and the rollout of SF₆-free solutions supported growth. Buildings delivered good growth
overall, led by strength in Non-residential which benefitted from effective commercial actions and
continued digital acceleration across distribution channels, while Residential growth was more
subdued, and varied by country. Among major economies, growth was led by Germany, up strong
double-digit, driven by Data Center and P&G. The U.K. also delivered double-digit growth with strong
contribution from Buildings, Industry and Infrastructure. France grew high-single digit led by Data
Center, while Italy was up mid-single digit driven by strong momentum in Infrastructure. Spain
delivered low-single digit growth against a high base of comparison. Across the rest of the region,
growth was high-single digit in aggregate, driven by strong momentum in the Nordics, reflecting
ongoing Data Center project execution.
Industrial Automation grew +6.0% organic. Growth was led by AVEVA, which was up strong double-
digit, driven by renewals of several multi-year subscription contracts, both on-premise and SaaS,
notably in Germany, Switzerland, U.K. and Norway. Sales into both Discrete and Process & Hybrid
automation markets grew low-single digit across the region. By country, the U.K. grew double-digit,
driven by strong performance at AVEVA and supported by strong growth in Discrete automation.
Germany and Spain each delivered high-single digit growth, with Germany benefitting from strong
growth at AVEVA and in Discrete Automation while Spain saw strong growth in Process & Hybrid.
France was around flat with growth at AVEVA and in Process & Hybrid automation offset by weakness
in Discrete automation. Italy was down slightly against a strong double-digit base of comparison. The
rest of Europe grew high-single digit in aggregate, supported by good traction in Discrete automation.
China & East Asia (19% of Q3 revenues) grew +26.1% organic in Q3.
Energy Management grew +32.4% organic. China grew strong double-digit with investment in AI
infrastructure benefitting several segments. The Data Center segment led growth, both from direct
sales to large customers in social media, technology and digital infrastructure and also with domestic
and regional co-location customers. The Semiconductor segment drove growth in the Industry end-
market, both direct and through OEMs. The Buildings and Infrastructure end-markets were weaker,
though the Group has reduced its exposure in Buildings over time, and renewable power generation
delivered growth within Infrastructure. East Asia grew strong double-digit, with growth led by Malaysia,
Thailand and Indonesia, each benefitting from very strong growth on data center projects, while
growth in South Korea and Taiwan was driven by the Semiconductor segment. Elsewhere in East Asia,
there was good traction in Industry and Infrastructure projects, compensating for a less dynamic
trend in Buildings.
Industrial Automation grew +8.1% organic, led by double-digit growth in Discrete automation, while
sales in Process & Hybrid markets and at AVEVA declined. China was up high single-digit, primarily
due to strong performance in Discrete automation markets, with strong growth among export OEMs
and an improving trend in the domestic market, tied with AI infrastructure buildout, while sales in
Process & Hybrid declined. East Asia grew mid-single digit, with strong growth in Process automation
led by Thailand, strong growth in Semiconductor notably in Japan, while AVEVA was down slightly due
to timing of renewals.

Financial Information
Page | 6
South Asia & International (18% of Q3 revenues) grew +13.2% organic in Q3.
Energy Management grew +16.0% organic. India delivered strong double-digit growth, with broad-
based strength across all four end-markets, including particularly strong contributions in Data Center
and for backup power and storage for Residential markets. The Middle East & Africa grew double-
digit. The Middle East delivered double-digit growth, despite the ongoing geopolitical and
macroeconomic tensions in the region, benefitting from strong growth in Data Center, supported by
strong momentum with channel partners. Africa was up mid-single digit. Australia grew double-digit,
where the Data Center segment continued to be the main driver of growth. South America was down
low-single digit, with Chile notably facing a high base of comparison from project execution in Q3’25.
Industrial Automation grew +3.0% organic. India delivered strong double-digit growth, driven primarily
by Discrete automation, and supported by the successful development of core product platforms
alongside localized portfolio adaptation. South America delivered double-digit growth, led by AVEVA
and supported by strong growth in both Discrete and Process & Hybrid automation, notably through
E&C project execution in Brazil. Australia was down double-digit, mainly reflecting a specific contract
renewal at AVEVA, while traditional automation markets were around flat. The Middle East & Africa saw
a high-single digit decline, where the timing of renewals at AVEVA impacted growth in some Gulf
countries, and Egypt faced a high base of comparison from project execution in the prior year.
SCOPE1 AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE2 IMPACTS IN Q3
In Q3, net acquisitions/disposals had an impact of -€36 million or -0.4% of Group revenues, mainly
reflecting the impact of some small disposals.
Based on transactions completed to-date, the Scope impact on FY 2026 revenues is estimated to be
around -€50 million. The Scope impact on adjusted EBITA margin for FY 2026 is estimated to be
around flat.
In Q3, the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations was positive at +€114 million or +1.2% of Group
revenues, mostly driven by the strengthening of the Chinese Yuan and the U.S. Dollar against the Euro,
partly offset by the weakening of the Indian Rupee against the Euro.
Based on current rates3, the FX impact on FY 2026 revenues is estimated to be between -€300 million
to -€400 million. The FX impact at current rates on adjusted EBITA margin for FY 2026 could be around
flat.
1. Changes in scope of consolidation also include some minor reclassifications of offers among different businesses.
2. For those currencies meeting the criteria to be considered hyperinflationary under IAS 29, such as Argentina and Türkiye, an IFRS
technical adjustment for hyperinflation impact is reflected as FX and therefore excluded from the organic growth calculation. The effect of
operational actions taken in these countries such as increased pricing to mitigate the inflationary impact is reflected as part of the
organic growth.
3. Forward exchange rates are volatile and difficult to predict. Consequently, the impact of such movement and possible impacts from
hyperinflation technical accounting (IAS29) are not factored at this stage.

II. SUSTAINABILITY IMPACT 2030
Schneider Electric continued to advance its ambitions across the four strategic pillars of the Group’s
sustainability roadmap, combining progress across its own operations with impact delivered through
its offers, value chain, people and communities. The Group’s Impact score reached 4.04, on track
toward the 2026 target of 4.20/10 (10/10 being the 2030 ambition).
Electrifying the World: Invest in breakthrough solutions and lead the Energy Tech transition by
deploying electrification and digitalization, starting with ourselves and scaling for all.
• Schneider Electric continued to decarbonize its operations in Q3, with Scopes 1 and 2 CO₂
emissions reduced by 83% compared to 2017.
• In the first nine months of 2026, Schneider Electric's solutions enabled customers to save or
electrify 211 million MWh.
Reinventing our Industry: Engage and elevate the entire value chain to set new standards in the
industry by rethinking how we design, source and promote, and engaging suppliers for decent work
and decarbonization.
Schneider Electric accelerated progress across its value chain in the third quarter.
• Building on a decade of supplier decarbonization efforts, Schneider Electric is scaling The Zero
Carbon Pathway (TZCP) program, with a ninefold increase in the number of suppliers
qualifying under the program, from 15 in the first half of 2026 (H1), to 135 suppliers at the end
of Q3. This marks progress toward the Group’s ambition of 1,500 qualifying suppliers by 2030.
• Responsible materials reached 22% across the materials and components covered by the
program (steel, aluminium, thermoplastics, electronics, electrical components, and
packaging) which assesses key materials against environmental and social criteria,
including lower embodied carbon, circularity and responsible supply-chain practices.
Unlocking Human Potential: Open the way to progress and shared prosperity by securing energy
access for all and investing in skills and people opportunities.
• Schneider Electric has helped 69 million people gain access to sustainable electricity since
2009 with 1.9 million additional people reached compared to H1 results.
• The Group has also equipped 1.5 million young people with skills to advance electrification
and sustainability since 2009, including 90,000 additional people since H1, progressing
toward its ambition of 3 million by 2030.
Empowering local communities: Promote local ecosystems and amplify grassroots voices by turning
sites into community anchors and empowering our people to be agents of change.
• The Group’s Impact Workplaces initiative accelerated sharply in Q3, growing from 5 sites in
the first half of the year to 59 sites at the end of Q3. The program applies a multi-criteria
framework spanning climate, resource efficiency, people and communities, as Schneider
Electric advances toward its ambition of 100 Impact Workplaces by 2030.
• In line with the Group’s conviction that global sustainability impact must be rooted locally,
Schneider Electric is empowering its people to drive impact in the communities where they

live and work. By the end of Q3, 9% of employees have engaged as Change Agents, with more
than 6,000 additional employees completing a volunteering activity during the quarter and
the program expanding from 49 to 57 countries.
“The strong results we are seeing nine months into Impact 2030 reinforce our conviction that
advancing Energy Tech can power progress for all. Sustainable progress demands that we bring
entire ecosystems along with us and build the capabilities needed to turn new technologies into
positive outcomes for people, businesses and communities,” said Esther Finidori, Chief Sustainability
Officer at Schneider Electric. “From scaling electrification and supplier decarbonization, to investing
in skills and strengthening the role of our people and sites in their local communities, we see
momentum across multiple Impact 2030 programs, and we look forward to accelerating these
further in the quarters ahead.”

III. PORTFOLIO UPDATES
Acquisitions
• PTC Inc. (“PTC”)
As separately announced, on October 5, 2026, Schneider Electric and PTC Inc., a leader in
complex industrial product design, engineering and data management, announced that they
have signed a definitive agreement under which Schneider Electric will acquire PTC. The
transaction will create a leading, scaled, open and interoperable industrial software and AI
franchise, driving business outcomes for customers from any system of design, control, data
and intelligence.
Subject to completion of the closing conditions, PTC shareholders will receive $205 per share
in cash. The transaction values 100% of PTC equity at approximately $22.6 billion, which implies
a $23.7 billion enterprise value. Schneider Electric is focused on delivering disciplined
shareholder value creation and expects to achieve €250 million of highly executable cost
synergies by Year 3 and approximately €800 million of revenue synergies.
Schneider Electric estimates the transaction would be accretive across key metrics, including
revenue growth, recurring revenue mix, gross margin, Adjusted EBITA margin and free cash
flow conversion. Schneider Electric expects the transaction to be immediately low single-digit
accretive to Adj. EPS (before PPA4) in the first year of full consolidation and mid-to high-single-
digit accretive to Adj. EPS (before PPA) including full run-rate synergies.
The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both
companies. Closing of the transaction is anticipated by Q3 2027, subject to customary closing
conditions, including approval by PTC’s shareholders holding at least a majority of
outstanding PTC shares at a special shareholder meeting and receipt of required regulatory
approvals. The PTC Board of Directors resolved to recommend that the Company’s
shareholders approve the Merger Agreement.
• Shelly Group (“Shelly”)
As separately announced, on September 24, 2026, Schneider Electric reached an agreement
with Shelly and its two founding shareholders, for the acquisition by way of a voluntary tender
offer for 100% of the shares of Shelly, providing all shareholders with a guaranteed liquidity
event and a one-time opportunity to realize immediate and certain value in cash, in an all-
cash transaction valued at approximately €1.2 bn.
Shelly is a provider of IoT and smart building solutions and the acquisition would combine
Shelly’s software-led home energy platform with Schneider Electric's technology leadership
across residential, retrofit and small commercial buildings.
Completion of the offer will be subject to Schneider Electric owning more than 95% of the
outstanding share capital of Shelly, with a view to proceeding to squeeze out and delist. The
transaction is also subject to customary regulatory approvals and is expected to close by Q1
2027.

IV. FINANCING UPDATE
Credit ratings
Following the announcement on October 5, 2026 of the definitive agreement for the
acquisition of PTC, on October 6, 2026 both S&P Global Ratings and Moody’s reaffirmed
Schneider Electric’s category-A credit ratings, maintaining A / A-1 (Stable) and A2 (Stable)
ratings, respectively.
The Group remains committed to retaining category-A credit ratings.
V. SHARE BUYBACK
In March 2026, Schneider Electric appointed Natixis to execute a share buyback program with a target
amount of €600 million, to be completed by November 2026. Execution is progressing in line with
expectations and remains on track for completion by the end of November.
As of September 30, 2026, the Group had purchased 1.6 million shares for €440 million at an average
price of €270 per share.
As of October 12, 2026 (the latest practicable date before this release), the Group has purchased 1.8
million shares for €497 million at an average price of €269 per share.
In line with its recent announcement, Schneider Electric remains committed to its share buyback
program of €2.5-€3.5 billion through 2030. The Group expects a pause in 2027 and 2028 with
acceleration thereafter, before completion of the program by the end of 2030 within the envelope
previously announced.

VII. EXPECTED TRENDS FOR Q4
Maintaining strong execution and operational discipline to achieve our upgraded FY26 target in a
dynamic environment:
• All four end-markets to drive growth
• Data Center & Networks to sustain strong momentum; Industry and Infrastructure to
contribute strongly; Buildings expected to track macroeconomic trends
• Systems to lead growth; strong Products growth supported by continued pricing momentum
• Sustained momentum in recurring Software revenues; accelerating growth in Services
• All four regions to deliver topline increase, led by U.S., China and India
• Disruption in the Middle East may impact Q4, with potential for pressure on global supply
chains and increased inflation
• Disciplined execution of Company program
• Continued pricing momentum expected to offset the value impact of raw material inflation
and net tariffs in FY26
• Productivity and operating leverage to contribute positively to adj. EBITA margin
VIII. 2026 TARGET UPGRADED
The Group upgrades its 2026 financial target as follows:
2026 Adjusted EBITA growth of between +18% and +21% organic.
The target would be achieved through a combination of organic revenue growth and margin
improvement, currently expected to be:
• Revenue growth of +12% to +14% organic
• Adjusted EBITA margin up +100bps to +120bps organic
This implies Adjusted EBITA margin of around 19.7% to 19.9% (including scope based on transactions
completed to-date and FX based on current estimation).

About Schneider Electric
Schneider Electric is a global energy technology leader, driving efficiency and sustainability by electrifying,
automating, and digitalizing industries, businesses, and homes. Its technologies enable buildings, data centers,
factories, infrastructure, and grids to operate as open, interconnected ecosystems, enhancing performance,
resilience, and sustainability. The portfolio includes intelligent devices, software-defined architectures, AI-
powered systems, digital services, and expert advisory. With 160,000 employees and 1 million partners in over 100
countries, Schneider Electric is consistently ranked among the world’s most sustainable companies.
